neighbours.label: a bare economic indicator noun (prices, taxes, wages, unemployment) as the subject of a short clause reporting its level or movement ('prices were higher', 'taxes were too low'), at the noun or its verb
fire: The village had one store and no bank. Prices were steep and choice was poor.
The crisis deepened that winter; wages fell and thousands lost their homes.
Roads were few and taxes were too light to fund any schools.
Markets there sell fresh fish daily, but prices are higher than in the port.
Factories closed across the north, and unemployment was worse than ever.
The harvest failed twice. Food prices doubled and rents kept climbing.
Jobs were scarce in the valley, and wages were lower than on the coast.
The boom ended suddenly; rents dropped and inflation was no longer a worry.
quiet: The village had one store and no bank. Children were playing by the well.
The storm deepened that night; branches fell and thousands lost their power.
Roads were few and the hills were too steep to cross by cart.
Markets there sell fresh fish daily, but tourists are fonder of the port.
Factories closed across the north, and the chimneys were quiet at last.
The harvest failed twice. The farmer sighed and his sons kept digging.
He wrote the prices on a slate and hung it by the door.
The clerk added the taxes to the bill and handed it over.

notes: Probes: 'Prices were higher' 0.92, 'prices dropped' 0.76, 'taxes were too low' 0.68, 'unemployment is no longer' 0.57, 'Crime rates are higher' 0.26, 'Symptoms may fade' 0.18, 'The price of the ticket was printed' 0.15. Two near misses keep the indicator word but as an object, not a level-reporting subject. wages/rents/inflation are untried.
